review_note: These are the only words the system is allowed to put in front of a customer, and they are reviewable here as flat text rather than inside code. The pipeline fills slots; it does not invent sentences. Changing a template is a compliance change, tracked in git.

templates.subject: We have opened an investigation — case {{CASE_ID}}
About the fees on your account — case {{CASE_ID}}
must_not_state: that the fee will be refunded

templates.subject: We have your message — case {{CASE_ID}}
must_not_state: a guarantee of any specific relief

templates.subject: We received your complaint — case {{CASE_ID}}

deferred_slots_note: These two slots are deliberately left UNFILLED by the pipeline. The customer's name is PII and is resolved from the system of record at send time, inside the bank's network; the analyst name is whoever approves the draft. A draft sitting in the review queue therefore contains no customer identity at all. Every other slot must be filled before QA will pass the draft.
issue_topics_note: What the letter says the complaint is ABOUT. An earlier version spliced the customer's own first sentence into the template, which produced ungrammatical letters ('thank you for writing to us about I had three overdraft fees...') and dropped redaction placeholders into customer-facing text. These are compliance-approved topic phrases instead: neutral, grammatical, and they characterise the subject without paraphrasing the customer's account of events or conceding anything. The analyst still sees the customer's own words in the console.
